inspiration.observed_pattern: A recursive CTE first selects a bounded newest set of parent rows, recursively labels descendants with their root, aggregates per-root reply counts and latest activity, then joins the statistics back to the selected roots while restoring chronological output order.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a support-ticket note report with independently named tables, concrete board and ticket filters, and a fixed newest-root limit. The recursive membership walk is tenant-scoped, the grouped statistics include each root's descendant count and latest note date, and the final ascending order demonstrates restoration after newest-first bounded selection.

fixture_notes: Ticket 700 on board 9 has three roots; the two newest roots are selected, their descendants are counted recursively, and output is restored to chronological root order. A child with a matching parent ID on board 8 is excluded by the board predicate. Ticket 701 and unrelated board 10 rows exercise the scope filters without affecting the report.
determinism_notes: Note IDs, board and ticket filters, timestamps, root limit, recursive join predicates, aggregate columns, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE support_notes (note_id INT PRIMARY KEY, board_id INT NOT NULL, ticket_id INT NOT NULL, parent_id INT NULL, author VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, body VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL, created_at DATETIME NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH RECURSIVE selected_roots AS (SELECT n.note_id, n.created_at FROM support_notes AS n WHERE n.board_id = 9 AND n.ticket_id = 700 AND n.parent_id IS NULL ORDER BY n.created_at DESC, n.note_id DESC LIMIT 2), membership(note_id, root_id, note_created_at) AS (SELECT sr.note_id, sr.note_id AS root_id, sr.created_at FROM selected_roots AS sr UNION ALL SELECT child.note_id, m.root_id, child.created_at FROM support_notes AS child INNER JOIN membership AS m ON child.parent_id = m.note_id WHERE child.board_id = 9 AND child.ticket_id = 700), thread_stats AS (SELECT root_id, COUNT(*) - 1 AS reply_count, MAX(note_created_at) AS last_activity_at FROM membership GROUP BY root_id) SELECT n.note_id, n.ticket_id, n.author, ts.reply_count, ts.last_activity_at FROM selected_roots AS sr INNER JOIN support_notes AS n ON n.note_id = sr.note_id INNER JOIN thread_stats AS ts ON ts.root_id = sr.note_id WHERE n.board_id = 9 AND n.ticket_id = 700 ORDER BY n.created_at ASC, n.note_id ASC

checks.sql: SELECT note_id, board_id, ticket_id, parent_id FROM support_notes ORDER BY note_id
